Figure $\mathrm{S}$ is made from four paper ribbons $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ wide. Each of the ribbons is $25 \mathrm{~cm}$ longer than the previous one (see the picture). By how many centimetres will the perimeter of figure $\mathrm{T}$ (made from the same ribbons) exceed that of figure $\mathrm{S}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, figure S is composed of four vertical paper strips of equal width placed side by side, with the bottom edges on the same straight line, and the heights of the paper strips increasing in order from left to right. Figure T is also composed of the same four paper strips placed side by side, with the bottom edges on the same line; the order of heights from left to right is the third shortest, the second shortest, the longest, and the shortest. Reasoning: Let the heights of the four paper strips from short to long be a, a+25, a+50, a+75. Each paper strip has width 10 cm, and S and T both use the same four paper strips, so the total contribution of horizontal edges is the same, and only the vertical outer edge lengths need to be compared. For adjacent vertical rectangles with a common bottom, the total length of vertical outer edges = left outer side height + right outer side height + the sum of the absolute values of adjacent height differences. The vertical total length of S is a+(a+75)+25+25+25=2a+150. The vertical total length of T is (a+50)+a+25+50+75=2a+200. Therefore, the perimeter of T is (2a+200)-(2a+150)=50 cm more than that of S.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: in figure S the four equal-width vertical ribbons stand side by side in increasing height order from left to right. In figure T, the same four heights appear in the order: third-shortest, second-shortest, tallest, shortest. From the text, each ribbon is 10 cm wide and consecutive ribbon lengths differ by 25 cm. Let the heights be a, a+25, a+50, a+75. Use the skyline perimeter formula for adjacent vertical rectangles with a common bottom: horizontal contribution is the same for S and T, so only compare exposed vertical segments: left outer height + right outer height + absolute height differences between neighboring ribbons. For S this vertical total is a+(a+75)+25+25+25. For T it is (a+50)+a+25+50+75. The difference is 50, so T exceeds S by 50 cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: S places the four ribbons side by side in increasing height order, while T rearranges them so the neighboring pairs are: third-shortest next to second-shortest, second-shortest next to tallest, and tallest next to shortest. From the text, denote the four ribbon heights as a, a+25, a+50, a+75, all width 10. Start with the sum of the four individual rectangle perimeters, which is identical for S and T. When two ribbons touch, the shared vertical edge is not part of the outside perimeter, so subtract twice the shared length, where the shared length is the smaller of the two adjacent heights. In S the total shared length is a+(a+25)+(a+50). In T it is (a+25)+(a+25)+a. Since T has 25 cm less total shared contact than S, its perimeter is larger by twice that, namely 50 cm.

推理：设四条纸带的高度依次为 a, a+25, a+50, a+75，宽度都是 10 cm。四个单独长方形的周长总和在 S 和 T 中相同。把纸带并排接触时，每一对相邻纸带的公共竖直边不计入外周长，因此要从单独周长总和中减去公共接触长度的 2 倍。

在 S 中，相邻公共边长度分别为 a, a+25, a+50，总公共长度为 3a+75。
在 T 中，相邻公共边长度分别为 a+25, a+25, a，总公共长度为 3a+50。

所以 S 的公共接触总长度比 T 多 25 cm。公共接触每少 1 cm，外周长就多 2 cm，因此 T 的周长比 S 多 2×25=50 cm。
